questions.question: Where is `Session.request` defined?
questions.notes: Exact identifier. Session.request builds a Request, prepares it with prepare_request, merges environment settings and calls self.send (sessions.py:622-653). Wrong but plausible: api.request (the module-level wrapper that opens a Session and calls session.request, api.py:70-71), the Request class in models.py, Session.send.

questions.question: Where is the top-level `requests.get` function defined?
questions.notes: 'get' collides with many symbols. requests.get is api.get (re-exported in __init__.py:171), which returns request("get", url, params=params, **kwargs) (api.py:87). Session.get is the session method (related, not the top-level function). Wrong but plausible: Session.get, RequestsCookieJar.get (cookies.py:211), LookupDict.get (structures.py:123-130).

questions.question: Which method raises an exception when a response has a 4xx or 5xx status code?
questions.notes: No identifier in the question. raise_for_status builds the 'Client Error' / 'Server Error' message and raises HTTPError (models.py:1160-1171). Response.ok calls it and catches HTTPError (related). Wrong but plausible: Response.ok / __bool__ (they return False instead of raising), HTTPAdapter.send (raises transport errors, not status errors), HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401.

questions.question: Which class makes header lookups case-insensitive?
questions.notes: Describes one class. CaseInsensitiveDict stores key.lower() -> (original key, value) in _store (structures.py:59-62); request and response headers are CaseInsensitiveDicts (models.py:568, adapters.py:382). Wrong but plausible: LookupDict in the same file (status codes), RequestsCookieJar (dict-like cookies), default_headers.

questions.question: Where does the HTTP adapter send a prepared request?
questions.notes: 'send' collides with several symbols. HTTPAdapter.send gets a pool connection, sets TLS options, resolves the timeout and calls conn.urlopen (adapters.py:695-708), maps urllib3 errors, then build_response (748). Wrong but plausible: BaseAdapter.send (abstract, raises NotImplementedError at 151), SessionRedirectMixin.send (a typing stub at sessions.py:132), Session.send (picks the adapter and calls adapter.send at 784; related).

questions.question: What happens when I call close on a response?
questions.notes: 'close' collides with Session.close, HTTPAdapter.close and BaseAdapter.close. Response.close closes raw if the content was not consumed and calls raw.release_conn() to give the connection back to the pool (models.py:1179-1184). Wrong but plausible: Session.close (closes adapters, sessions.py:883-886), HTTPAdapter.close (clears the PoolManager), BaseAdapter.close (abstract).

questions.question: Digest kimlik doğrulaması hangi sınıfta yapılıyor?
questions.notes: Describes one class in Turkish. HTTPDigestAuth(AuthBase): __call__ registers handle_401 as a response hook (auth.py:339), handle_401 parses the WWW-Authenticate challenge and resends, build_digest_header computes the digest (MD5/SHA/SHA-256/SHA-512). Methods inside the class overlap its range and count. Wrong but plausible: HTTPBasicAuth, HTTPProxyAuth, _basic_auth_str.

questions.question: post istegi gonderen fonksiyon nerede tanimli?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('POST isteği gönderen fonksiyon nerede tanımlı'); 'post' collides with an ordinary word. Either requests.post (api.py:117-134, calls request("post", ...)) or Session.post (sessions.py:695-712, calls self.request("POST", ...)) answers it. Wrong but plausible: SessionRedirectMixin.rebuild_method (turns POST into GET on 301), PreparedRequest.prepare_method, prepare_body.

questions.question: How does requests decide which proxy to use for a given URL?
questions.notes: select_proxy tries the keys scheme://host, scheme, all://host, all in order (utils.py:896-906); resolve_proxies adds the environment proxy for the scheme unless NO_PROXY says to bypass (926-939). Session.send calls resolve_proxies (sessions.py:763) and the adapter calls select_proxy (adapters.py:483). Wrong but plausible: HTTPAdapter.proxy_manager_for (builds the manager for an already chosen proxy), HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers, HTTPProxyAuth.

questions.question: How is the text encoding of a response guessed when the server does not declare a charset?
questions.notes: Without a charset parameter get_encoding_from_headers returns ISO-8859-1 for text/* and utf-8 for application/json, else None (utils.py:583-591; called from build_response, adapters.py:385). When encoding is None, Response.text falls back to apparent_encoding (models.py:1074-1075), which runs chardet/charset_normalizer detect (899-904). Any of the three answers. Wrong but plausible: get_encodings_from_content and get_unicode_from_response (deprecated, unused), stream_decode_response_unicode, guess_json_utf (JSON only).

questions.question: When a redirect goes to a different host, where is the Authorization header removed?
questions.notes: rebuild_auth deletes headers['Authorization'] when should_strip_auth(original_url, url) is true (sessions.py:324-327); should_strip_auth compares hostnames and allows http->https on default ports (158-184). resolve_redirects calls rebuild_auth (273). Wrong but plausible: rebuild_proxies (Proxy-Authorization), HTTPDigestAuth.handle_redirect (resets a counter), prepare_auth.

questions.question: How can I point requests at a custom CA bundle with an environment variable?
questions.notes: With trust_env and verify True/None, merge_environment_settings reads REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, then CURL_CA_BUNDLE (sessions.py:855-860); Session.request calls it (641-643). Wrong but plausible: certs.where / DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH (the certifi default, utils.py:81-82), get_environ_proxies (environment proxies), HTTPAdapter.cert_verify (uses the value, does not read the environment).

questions.question: Zaman aşımı (timeout) tek bir sayı ya da (bağlantı, okuma) ikilisi olarak verildiğinde nasıl işleniyor?
questions.notes: The answer is a few lines inside HTTPAdapter.send: a (connect, read) tuple becomes urllib3 Timeout (TimeoutSauce), a Timeout object passes through, a single value is used for both (adapters.py:681-693); ConnectTimeoutError / ReadTimeoutError become ConnectTimeout / ReadTimeout (714-717, 741-742). The whole method is the expected symbol because the search returns symbols. Wrong but plausible: the Timeout exception classes in exceptions.py, Session.request (only forwards timeout in send_kwargs).

questions.question: Dosya yuklerken multipart govdesi nasil olusturuluyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('Dosya yüklerken multipart gövdesi nasıl oluşturuluyor'). _encode_files turns data fields and 2/3/4-tuple files into urllib3 RequestFields and calls urllib3's encode_multipart_formdata (models.py:199-251); prepare_body calls it when files are given (636-637, related). The boundary encoding itself is urllib3's. Wrong but plausible: _encode_params (urlencoded form body), prepare_body alone, prepare_content_length.

questions.question: What is the call path from requests.get(url) down to the transport adapter that sends it?
questions.notes: api.get -> api.request opens a Session and calls session.request (api.py:70-71); Session.request builds a Request, prepare_request merges session settings into a PreparedRequest, merge_environment_settings adds env proxies/CA bundle, then self.send (sessions.py:622-653); Session.send picks the adapter with get_adapter (778) and calls adapter.send (784), i.e. HTTPAdapter.send. Session.request and Session.send are required; the wrappers and HTTPAdapter.send are related. Wrong but plausible: Session.get (the session method, not the top-level path), Request.prepare.

questions.question: `Session.send` yönlendirmeleri (redirect) nasıl takip ediyor?
questions.notes: Exact identifier in a Turkish question. With allow_redirects, Session.send runs self.resolve_redirects(r, request, **kwargs) and builds history (sessions.py:801-815). resolve_redirects loops while get_redirect_target finds a Location: copies the request, enforces max_redirects (TooManyRedirects, 216-219), resolves relative URLs, rebuild_method, drops the body except on 307/308, re-prepares cookies, rebuild_proxies / rebuild_auth, rewinds the body and calls self.send(..., allow_redirects=False) (186-307). Both required. Wrong but plausible: Response.is_redirect alone, HTTPDigestAuth.handle_redirect, HTTPAdapter.send (redirect=False there).

questions.question: Istege verilen cookie'ler session cookie'leriyle nasil birlestirilip Cookie basligina yaziliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('İsteğe verilen cookie'ler session cookie'leriyle nasıl birleştirilip Cookie başlığına yazılıyor'). prepare_request turns request cookies into a jar and merges session cookies, then request cookies, into a new RequestsCookieJar (sessions.py:524-533) and passes it to PreparedRequest.prepare (552); prepare_cookies calls get_cookie_header (MockRequest + CookieJar.add_cookie_header) and sets headers['Cookie'] (models.py:712-720). Both required. Wrong but plausible: extract_cookies_to_jar (response -> jar, the other direction), the cookie persistence in Session.send (793-799), RequestsCookieJar.set.

questions.question: How are connections pooled and reused across requests to the same host?
questions.notes: Pooling is urllib3's PoolManager / HTTPConnectionPool. requests only creates PoolManager(num_pools, maxsize, block) in init_poolmanager (adapters.py:262-267) and asks it for a pool with connection_from_host (501-508); release back to the pool is raw.release_conn in Response.close. Correct behaviour: say the pool implementation is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: Session.mount / get_adapter (adapter selection, not pooling), HTTPAdapter class docstring.

questions.question: Where is the server's TLS certificate checked against the CA bundle during the handshake?
questions.notes: The handshake and certificate verification happen in urllib3 / Python's ssl; the CA bundle comes from certifi. requests only passes settings: _urllib3_request_context builds cert_reqs CERT_REQUIRED/CERT_NONE and ca_certs/ca_cert_dir pool kwargs (adapters.py:97-105), cert_verify sets the same on the connection and checks the bundle path exists (321-346). Correct behaviour: say verification is not in the repo and cite these. Wrong but plausible: SSLError in exceptions.py, the docstrings about verify in Session.request.

questions.question: Bağlantı koparsa istek nasıl yeniden deneniyor, yeniden deneme döngüsü nerede?
questions.notes: No identifier. The retry loop is urllib3's Retry. HTTPAdapter.__init__ sets max_retries = Retry(0, read=False) by default (DEFAULT_RETRIES = 0, adapters.py:81) or Retry.from_int (208-211); HTTPAdapter.send passes retries=self.max_retries to conn.urlopen (705) and maps MaxRetryError to ConnectTimeout / RetryError / ProxyError / SSLError / ConnectionError (713-729). Correct behaviour: say the retry logic is not in the repo (and that requests does not retry by default) and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: resolve_redirects (a loop, but for redirects), HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 (resends once after a 401).
